description:
Advances: specled.compiler_tracer

[BUG] `bootstrap_tracer!/0` in `mix.exs` can permanently run a STALE tracer beam that no `mix compile --force` can heal, because the tracer source is deliberately excluded from `elixirc_paths` and its only staleness check is a strictly-greater, second-granularity mtime comparison.

Found 2026-07-26 while orchestrating epic specled_-233. It produced a real false failure — a red `make smoke` on specled_-ymn that looked exactly like a genuine cross-VM-uniqueness regression, and cost a full root-cause investigation to clear.

## Mechanism

`mix.exs`:

    @tracer_source "lib/specled_ex/compiler/tracer.ex"

    defp lib_paths do
      Path.wildcard("lib/**/*.ex") |> Enum.reject(&(&1 == @tracer_source))
    end

The tracer source is REJECTED from `elixirc_paths` — correctly, since it is the compiler tracer and cannot be traced by its own compilation. So `mix compile`, including `mix compile --force`, never rebuilds it. It is built solely by:

    defp bootstrap_tracer! do
      ...
      stale? =
        not File.regular?(beam) or
          File.stat!(src).mtime > File.stat!(beam).mtime
      if stale? do ... Kernel.ParallelCompiler.compile_to_path([src], ebin, ...) end

`File.stat!/1` mtime has ONE-SECOND granularity, and the comparison is strictly `>`. So if the source's mtime lands in the SAME SECOND as the existing beam's mtime, `stale?` is false and the beam is never rebuilt — regardless of content.

## How it fires in practice

Any edit-compile-revert cycle inside one second. Concretely, what happened here:

1. A reviewer mutated `lib/specled_ex/compiler/tracer.ex:342`, replacing `System.pid()` with a second `System.unique_integer([:positive])`, to falsify a test.
2. Running the suite invoked `bootstrap_tracer!`, which compiled the MUTATED source to `_build/test/lib/spec_led_ex/ebin/Elixir.SpecLedEx.Compiler.Tracer.beam`.
3. `git checkout -- lib/specled_ex/compiler/tracer.ex` restored the source. Git stamps the restored file with the checkout time, which landed in the same second as the beam.
4. `src.mtime > beam.mtime` was now FALSE. The mutated beam became permanently "fresh".

Observed state: source mtime and beam mtime both `Jul 26 20:14:22 2026`. `git status` clean, `git diff` vs base 0 bytes — the tree was pristine while the running code was mutated.

## Why it is nasty

- The source reads `System.pid()`; the loaded module executes two `unique_integer` calls. Reading the code tells you nothing.
- `mix compile --force` does NOT fix it (the file is excluded from the compile paths). This is the step everyone reaches for.
- Verified by decompiling the beam: `:beam_lib.chunks(beam, [:abstract_code])` showed line 342 compiled as `path <> ".tmp." <> unique_integer <> "_" <> unique_integer`, with no `System.pid` call anywhere.
- The resulting failure is maximally misleading. The test asserts a pid-bearing temp-name sibling; the observed sibling was `xref_mfa.etf.tmp.7_39`. That reads as a genuine loss of cross-VM uniqueness — the exact regression the test exists to catch — when in fact production code was correct and only the cached beam was wrong.
- Diagnostic tell, for anyone who hits it again: in the failing names both components differ by exactly the `unique_integer` stride (32 on this machine), e.g. `7_39`, `6_38`, `2442_2466`. A genuine `<pid>_<counter>` pair has no fixed relationship. If the two numbers differ by a constant across runs, both are counters and you are running a stale beam.

Workaround that resolved it: `touch lib/specled_ex/compiler/tracer.ex` (making src strictly newer), then re-run. Deleting the beam also works.

## Fix

Stop relying on mtime ordering. Options, best first:

1. Compare CONTENT, not timestamps: hash the source and store the hash alongside the beam (or read it back out of the beam's compile info), rebuild when the hash differs. Immune to same-second edits, clock skew, and checkouts.
2. Keep mtime but use `>=` instead of `>`, i.e. rebuild on tie. Cheap one-character fix that closes the same-second window, at the cost of an occasional redundant recompile of one file.
3. Compare against the beam's recorded source, e.g. `Keyword.get(SpecLedEx.Compiler.Tracer.module_info(:compile), :source)` plus a stored digest.

Also worth doing regardless: make the staleness decision observable. A one-line `Mix.shell().info/1` when the bootstrap decides to skip a rebuild would have made this self-diagnosing instead of a multi-step investigation.

## Test it properly

Whatever fix lands must be falsifiable, and mtime bugs are easy to "fix" untestably. Suggested regression test: write a mutated tracer source, compile it via the bootstrap, restore the original content while forcing both mtimes equal (`File.touch!(src, mtime)` with the beam's mtime), invoke the bootstrap, and assert the loaded module reflects the RESTORED source. That test must fail against the current `>` comparison.

comments.text:
Adopted into epic specled_-233 on the user's instruction (2026-07-27) so it ships on that epic's single PR. The epic branch already impacts specled.compiler_tracer via specled_-ymn, and mix.exs is on that subject's surface, so the bundling is coherent rather than opportunistic.

Implementation note before starting: bootstrap_tracer!/0 is a `defp` on SpecLedEx.MixProject, so the regression test this ticket demands cannot call it as written. Fix will take option 1 (content digest, not mtime) AND make the entry point testable by threading src/ebin as parameters, so the test can drive a real bootstrap against scratch paths and assert a rebuild happens when content changes with mtimes held EQUAL — the exact condition the current `>` comparison misses.

IMPLEMENTED and verified. Commit dd6dc1f6 on epic/specled_-233-impromptu-followups.

Files touched: mix.exs; test/specled_ex/compiler/tracer_bootstrap_test.exs (new);
.spec/specs/compiler_tracer.spec.md

FIX — took option 1 from this ticket (content digest), not option 2 (mtime `>=`). Staleness is
now decided by comparing a SHA-256 digest of the source against a digest recorded beside the
artifact, written ONLY after a successful compile so a failed compile leaves the artifact stale
instead of marking it fresh. Immune to mtime ties, ordering, and clock skew — option 2 would
only have closed the same-second window.

TESTABILITY — bootstrap_tracer!/0 was a `defp` on SpecLedEx.MixProject and therefore uncallable
from ExUnit, which is why this defect shipped untested. Extracted compile_tracer_if_stale!/3 as
a public, parameterised entry point so a test can drive a real bootstrap against scratch paths;
production still calls bootstrap_tracer!/0. Five tests added covering: first build, no-op on
unchanged content, rebuild on content change with mtimes forced EQUAL, rebuild when the source
is OLDER than the artifact, and no-digest-on-failed-compile.

FALSIFIABILITY PROVEN, not asserted. Reverted tracer_stale?/3 to
`File.stat!(src).mtime > File.stat!(beam).mtime` and re-ran: 2 of 5 tests FAILED — "rebuilds on
a content change even when source and beam mtimes are IDENTICAL" and "rebuilds when the source
is OLDER than the beam but its content differs". Restored the fix, confirmed zero mtime
comparisons remain in mix.exs, and re-ran green. This ticket warned that mtime bugs are easy to
fix untestably, so the proof was run before the commit rather than claimed after it.

SPEC WORK — added two requirements to specled.compiler_tracer, not one. The first draft bundled
content-digest staleness and digest-only-after-success into a single requirement covered by two
scenarios, which the gate correctly rejected as overlap/duplicate_covers. Split so each scenario
covers a distinct id: bootstrap_rebuilds_on_content_change and
bootstrap_digest_recorded_after_success, both wired into an execute:true tagged_tests entry, each
test tagged individually (an @tag would REPLACE an @moduletag value for the same key rather than
add to it).

Also removed a dangling reference: the first draft's @doc cited
`specled.decision.tracer_bootstrap_content_digest`, an ADR that does not exist. Judged the change
too local to warrant one; the reasoning is stated inline instead.

The new test's tmp root uses SpecLedEx.TempName.cross_vm_suffix/0 rather than a VM-local counter,
avoiding the nested-run hazard filed as specled_-ehv.

Full gate green on the epic branch:
  mix compile --warnings-as-errors  exit 0
  mix format --check-formatted      exit 0
  mix deps.unlock --check-unused    exit 0
  mix test                          3 properties, 1260 tests, 0 failures (was 1255)
  mix spec.check (bare)             spec.check result=pass; validate errors=0 warnings=0

title: bootstrap_tracer! can run a permanently stale tracer beam: same-second mtime tie defeats its staleness check and mix compile --force cannot heal it
